items.title: The far-field gradient of a compactly supported Newtonian potential
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the Lebesgue interface used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge3$, let $\Phi$ be the fundamental solution of $-\Delta$ on $\mathbb R^n$ normalised by $-\Delta T_\Phi=\delta_0$ ([[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]]), so that for $z\ne0$
$$\Phi(z)=\frac{|z|^{2-n}}{(n-2)\omega_{n-1}},\qquad \nabla\Phi(z)=-\frac{z}{\omega_{n-1}|z|^n},\qquad |\nabla\Phi(z)|=\frac{1}{\omega_{n-1}|z|^{n-1}},$$
let $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$ be real, measurable and zero $\lambda_n$-almost everywhere outside a closed ball $\overline B_R(0)=\{x:|x|\le R\}$ of finite radius $R>0$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), and let
$$Nf(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Phi(x-y)f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y)$$
be the Newtonian potential ([[def-newtonian-potential]]). Then:
(a) [Representation and differentiability off the far field] for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$ with $|x|>2R$ the integral $\int_{\mathbb R^n}\nabla\Phi(x-y)f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y)$ is absolutely convergent, the function $Nf$ is differentiable at $x$ with
$$\nabla(Nf)(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\nabla\Phi(x-y)f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y),$$
and $x\mapsto\nabla(Nf)(x)$ is continuous on the open set $\{x:|x|>2R\}$;
(b) [Decay bound] for every $x$ with $|x|>2R$,
$$|\nabla(Nf)(x)|\le\frac{2^{n-1}\|f\|_1}{\omega_{n-1}|x|^{n-1}},\qquad \|f\|_1:=\int_{\mathbb R^n}|f|\,d\lambda_n;$$
(c) [Scope] the hypothesis is compact support together with $L^1$-integrability; no boundedness of $f$ is assumed, and nothing is asserted at points with $|x|\le2R$ (where the kernel singularity may meet the support of $f$).

items.title: The distributional gradient of a locally integrable function smooth off one point
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) for the Lebesgue and product-measure interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $p\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$ be continuous on $\mathbb R^n\setminus\{p\}$ and of class $C^1$ there, with each classical partial derivative $\partial_iu:\mathbb R^n\setminus\{p\}\to\mathbb R$ (extended by $0$ at $p$) again in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$. Then for every $i=1,\dots,n$, with $T_u\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ the regular distribution of $u$ ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $\partial_i$ the distributional derivative ([[def-distributional-derivative]]),
$$\partial_iT_u=T_{\partial_iu}\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n),$$
that is, $\langle\partial_iT_u,\psi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_iu\,\psi\,d\lambda_n$ for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). The value assigned to $\partial_iu$ at the single point $p$ is immaterial, because a singleton is Lebesgue null ([[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]], [[thm-the-lebesgue-integral-respects-almost-everywhere-equality]]). Both hypotheses are used: $u$ must be locally integrable and continuous away from $p$, and each classical partial must be locally integrable; the lemma is asserted for one exceptional point, not for an exceptional set of positive surface measure.

items.title: Euclidean balls, annuli and spheres as bounded smooth domains and hypersurfaces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the boundary-chart and surface-measure interfaces used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). On $\mathbb R^3$ with its Euclidean structure ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) let $0<\varepsilon<R$ and put
$$B_R:=\{x:|x|<R\},\qquad \overline B_R:=\{x:|x|\le R\},\qquad A_{\varepsilon,R}:=\{x:\varepsilon<|x|<R\},\qquad S_r:=\{x:|x|=r\}.$$
Then:
(a) [Domains] $B_R$ and $A_{\varepsilon,R}$ are bounded $C^1$ domains in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]; their boundaries are $S_R$, respectively $S_\varepsilon\cup S_R$, and the corresponding outward unit normals are
$$\nu(x)=\frac{x}{|x|}\ \ (x\in S_R),\qquad \nu(x)=-\frac{x}{|x|}\ \ (x\in S_\varepsilon,\ \text{boundary of }A_{\varepsilon,R});$$
(b) [Spheres] each $S_r$ is a compact embedded $C^1$ (indeed $C^\infty$) hypersurface in the sense of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] with two-sided unit normals $\pm x/|x|$, and the boundary components $S_\varepsilon,S_R$, each subdivided into six compact signed-maximal-coordinate graph faces $F_{r,k,\sigma}:=\{x\in S_r:\sigma x_k\ge |x_j|\text{ for all }j\}$ ($k=1,2,3$, $\sigma=\pm1$), with the compact edge set consisting of their seams $\sigma x_k=|x_j|$ for $j\ne k$, give a finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of $A_{\varepsilon,R}$ in the sense of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]];
(c) [Consequences used downstream] the divergence theorem and Green's first identity of [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] and [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] apply on $B_R$ and on $A_{\varepsilon,R}$ with the outward normals of (a), and $S_r$ carries a finite Borel surface measure with the standard graph charts.

items.title: The static and pure electrostatic regimes and their fixed-time reading
items.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units, constants and symbols of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and let $(\rho,J)$ be source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$, all of class $C^1$ (with every additional derivative appearing below existing and continuous); $\partial_t$ is the partial time derivative at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].
(a) [Static regime] The **static (time-independent) electromagnetic regime** on $\Omega\times I$ is the requirement
$$\partial_tE=0,\qquad\partial_tB=0,\qquad\partial_t\rho=0,\qquad\partial_tJ=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$
(b) [Pure electrostatics] The **pure electrostatic regime** is the static regime together with $J=0$ and $B=0$ on $\Omega\times I$.
(c) [Reduced equations] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds in the static regime, then the four Maxwell equations reduce to
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, with $\operatorname{div}$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied at each fixed time; in the pure electrostatic regime the reduction is exactly the pair $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$.
(d) [Fixed-time reading] In the static regime $E,B,\rho,J$ do not depend on $t$, so each is the pullback along $(y,t)\mapsto y$ of a single map on $\Omega$; this fixed-time reading (the spatial field or source) is the object analysed by the electrostatic statements of this page, and no other time dependence is introduced. The equations of (c) are equations between those spatial maps.
(e) [Static-to-distributional reading] Let fields $E,B$ and volume densities $\rho,J$ be locally integrable and time independent on $\Omega\times I$, and let $\Omega$ be open. Then, under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the cited measure and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]), the weak equations of the solution predicate of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) for these time-independent objects hold if and only if the four spatial equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega)$; the passage between them is the integration in $t$ of the pairings against $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ tests, justified by [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] after identifying fields and densities with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). In particular a **stationary point charge** at $x_0\in\Omega$ with charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ is the point source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) with constant trajectory $z(t)\equiv x_0$, whose pairing is $\psi\mapsto q\int_I\psi(x_0,t)\,dt$ and whose fixed-time reading is the spatial point source $\eta\mapsto q\eta(x_0)$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).
(f) [Conventions and scope] The regime is imposed in the one inertial frame of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; no claim is made that time independence survives a change of inertial description, and where a frame change is used the transformed fields must be rechecked. The static regime is an adopted idealization, not a dynamical stability theorem: static charged matter requires external support or an adopted equilibrium model. No equation is asserted here for singular sources beyond the dictionary of (e), and no empirical claim is made.

items.title: Scalar potential and the Poisson equation in a star-shaped electrostatic region
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set that is star-shaped with respect to some $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]), let $E:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^1$ in the spatial vector-field sense of [[def-em-fields]] ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and let $\rho:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be continuous — the fixed-time reading, in the sense of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], of a pure electrostatic regime with the units and constant $\varepsilon_0>0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[def-em-sources]]). Suppose the reduced smooth-branch equations hold pointwise on $\Omega$:
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$
with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then:
(a) [Closed field and potential] $-E$ is closed in the sense of [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]] — equivalently $\operatorname{curl}(-E)=0$ ([[cor-curl-vanishes-exactly-when-a-field-is-closed]]) — and the function
$$\varphi(x):=-\int_0^1E\bigl(a+s(x-a)\bigr)\cdot(x-a)\,ds$$
(the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) is a $C^2$ function on $\Omega$ with
$$\nabla\varphi=-E\qquad\text{on }\Omega$$
([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-star-shaped-domains]] applied to the closed $C^1$ field $-E$; continuity of the integrand and its first parameter derivatives first gives $C^1$; the proved identity $\nabla\varphi=-E$ with $E\in C^1$ then gives $C^2$).
(b) [Poisson equation] with $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}\nabla\varphi$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]],
$$-\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0}\qquad\text{pointwise on }\Omega.$$
(c) [Uniqueness up to constants] if $\psi\in C^2(\Omega)$ satisfies $\nabla\psi=-E$ on $\Omega$, then $\psi-\varphi$ is constant on $\Omega$; in particular $\varphi$ is uniquely determined by $\nabla\varphi=-E$ and one prescribed value. (Star-shapedness gives path-connectedness through the centre $a$, so the constant is the same on all of $\Omega$; [[cor-potentials-differ-by-a-componentwise-constant]], [[def-piecewise-c1-path-connected-conservative-and-path-independent]].)
No normalisation of $\varphi$ at infinity, and no boundary condition, is asserted on a general star-shaped $\Omega$; the additive constant remains free.

items.title: The localized Newtonian potential and the ideal point-charge Coulomb field
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in $\mathbb R^3$ with its Euclidean structure ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}>0$. Let $\Phi$ be the $n=3$ fundamental solution of $-\Delta$ of [[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]], normalised by $-\Delta T_\Phi=\delta_0$; then $\omega_2=4\pi$ and
$$\Phi(z)=\frac{1}{4\pi|z|}\qquad(z\ne0)$$
([[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). Let $Nf$ be the Newtonian potential of [[def-newtonian-potential]].
(a) [Smooth compact sources] Let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ with compact support contained in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), put $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi$. Then $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[thm-newtonian-potential-for-holder-data-is-classical]]), and pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$
$$-\Delta\varphi=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0$$
with the operators of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]] and [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Moreover, with $Q:=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Coulomb integral representation holds, and its far-field bound holds for $|x|>2R$,
$$E(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{x-y}{|x-y|^3}\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(x\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad |E(x)|\le\frac{\| \rho\|_1}{\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2}\quad(|x|>2R),$$
and for $|x|>\max(2R,1)$ the potential obeys the decay bound $|\varphi(x)|\le\bigl(|Q|/(4\pi)+R\|\rho\|_1/\pi\bigr)/(\varepsilon_0|x|)$ ([[lem-em-newtonian-far-field-gradient]], [[thm-decay-of-the-newtonian-potential-of-compactly-supported-data]]). The pair $(E,0,\rho,0)$ therefore realises the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with source $\rho$, and $E$ is the field of the localised Newtonian potential.
(b) [Uniqueness with vanishing at infinity] If $\psi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies $-\Delta\psi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$ and $\lim_{|x|\to\infty}\psi(x)=0$, then $\psi=\varphi$ ([[thm-weak-maximum-principle-for-the-laplacian]]). In particular, among $C^2$ solutions of the Poisson equation of a compactly supported $C^1$ source decaying at infinity, the localised Newtonian potential is the unique one.
(c) [Compactly supported $L^1$ sources] If instead $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ is real, measurable and compactly supported, then $N\rho$ is finite $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere, belongs to $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, is $C^\infty$ and harmonic off the support of $\rho$, and its regular distribution satisfies
$$-\Delta T_{\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho}=T_{\rho/\varepsilon_0}\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
([[thm-newtonian-potential-solves-poisson-distributionally]], scaled by $\varepsilon_0^{-1}$; [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).
(d) [Point charge] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and define, with arbitrary values at $x_0$,
$$\varphi_q(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|},\qquad E_q(x):=\frac{q\,(x-x_0)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|^3}\qquad(x\ne x_0).$$
Then $\varphi_q\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, $E_q$ is locally integrable and $C^\infty$ off $x_0$, $E_q=-\nabla\varphi_q$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{x_0\}$, and, with $T_{\varphi_q}$ the regular distribution of $\varphi_q$ and $\operatorname{div}E_q:=\sum_i\partial_iT_{E_{q,i}}$, $\operatorname{curl}E_q:=(\partial_2T_{E_{q,3}}-\partial_3T_{E_{q,2}},\ \partial_3T_{E_{q,1}}-\partial_1T_{E_{q,3}},\ \partial_1T_{E_{q,2}}-\partial_2T_{E_{q,1}})$,
$$-\Delta T_{\varphi_q}=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\delta_{x_0},\qquad \operatorname{div}E_q=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\delta_{x_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E_q=0\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
([[thm-minus-laplacian-of-the-fundamental-solution-is-dirac]] for the first identity, [[lem-em-distributional-gradient-smooth-off-a-point]] for the passage from the potential to the field, [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]). The distribution $q\delta_{x_0}$ is the fixed-time reading of the stationary point charge of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) with charge parameter $q$ and constant trajectory $z\equiv x_0$ ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e)); so the pair $(E_q,0)$ satisfies the distributional pure electrostatic equations with that point source. This is an idealised point-source model: no claim of uniqueness for the point source, no self-force and no statement about the field at $x_0$ itself is made.

items.title: Work of the electrostatic force is the potential difference and is path independent
Finite-source assembly energy equals the electric field energy
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the Lebesgue, polar and surface interfaces cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\rho\in C^1_c(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ with support in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), let $\varphi=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ be the smooth-branch Coulomb solution of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](a) with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], and let $\Phi$ be the $n=3$ kernel, $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$ ([[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). Then:
(a) [Finiteness] the three quantities
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3,\qquad +\frac{1}{2\varepsilon_0}\iint_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3}\Phi(x-y)\rho(x)\rho(y)\,d(\lambda_3\times\lambda_3)(x,y)$$
are finite real numbers;
(b) [Identity] they are equal:
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon_0}\iint_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3}\Phi(x-y)\rho(x)\rho(y)\,d(\lambda_3\times\lambda_3)(x,y).$$
The last expression is the **external assembly work** of the ideal quasistatic bookkeeping family $\rho_s=s\rho$, $\varphi_s=s\varphi$ for $0\le s\le1$. An added test charge brought from infinity, where the potential is zero, has electric-force work $-dq\,\varphi_s$ by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-work]]; the balancing external work is $+dq\,\varphi_s$. Therefore $W_{\rm ext}=\int_0^1s\,ds\int\rho\varphi=\tfrac12\int\rho\varphi$. Both signs of $\rho$ are allowed. The symmetric double kernel gives the equivalent ordered-pair interpretation of the factor $1/2$.
(c) [Scope] the identity is a statement about the ideal quasi-static assembly of a compactly supported $C^1$ charge distribution in vacuum, all sources being held in place by external support ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]). It asserts no time-dependent work, no radiation, no material or stability model, and it does not identify the field energy with the rest mass of any particle; the point-source limit is treated separately and is divergent (see the point-charge field energy of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d)).

items.title: Divergence of the point-charge field energy and the limits of mass inference
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the Lebesgue and polar interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $q\in\mathbb R$, $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, and let $E_q$ be the ideal point-charge field of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d) ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). For $0<\delta<R$ put
$$U_q(\delta,R):=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\{\delta\le|x-x_0|\le R\}}|E_q(x)|^2\,d\lambda_3(x)$$
(the truncated field energy of the shell between the two spheres, [[def-metric-ball]]). Then:
(a) [Exact truncated energy] for all $0<\delta<R$,
$$U_q(\delta,R)=\frac{q^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0}\Bigl(\frac1\delta-\frac1R\Bigr);$$
(b) [Divergence] $\lim_{R\to\infty}U_q(\delta,R)=q^2/(8\pi\varepsilon_0\delta)$ for every $\delta>0$, and for $q\ne0$
$$\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}U_q(\delta,R)=+\infty\qquad\text{for every }R>0;$$
so the field energy of the ideal point charge is locally infinite at its own location, and any finite-energy treatment of a point-like charge must modify the source/field near the singularity or introduce an explicit cutoff;
(c) [Limits of the mass inference] the identity is a divergence of the *field energy of the idealised point source* in the framework's SI conventions. It does not assert that a physical particle has infinite rest mass, does not identify field energy with rest mass, contains no measurement, and involves neither a self-force nor a contradiction claim for classical electrodynamics: the framework supplies no mass-energy identification for a charged particle, and the smooth compact-source field/assembly energy of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] remains finite. The compact $L^1$ branch of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] retains its locally integrable potential and distributional Poisson equation; it does not guarantee finite field energy for arbitrary $L^1$ densities. The point source itself is the idealisation of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e)); its energy divergence is a mathematical property of that idealisation, not an empirical result.

items.title: The infinite line charge: logarithmic potential, flux normalization and divergent energy
The uniformly charged ball: interior and exterior fields, continuous potential and finite energy
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$, $Q\in\mathbb R$, let $\overline B_a=\{x:|x|\le a\}$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), and define, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]]),
$$\rho(x):=\frac{3Q}{4\pi a^3}\,\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<a\}}(x),\qquad
E(x):=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\begin{cases}x/a^3,&|x|<a,\\ x/|x|^3,&|x|\ge a,\end{cases}\qquad
\varphi(x):=\begin{cases}\dfrac{Q(3a^2-|x|^2)}{8\pi\varepsilon_0a^3},&|x|\le a,\\[6pt]\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x|},&|x|\ge a.\end{cases}$$
(The value of $\rho$ on the sphere $\{|x|=a\}$ is immaterial: it is a Lebesgue-null set by the polar calculation $\lambda_3(S_a)=4\pi\int_0^\infty\mathbf1_{\{a\}}(r)r^2dr=0$, since the one-dimensional singleton has measure zero ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]], [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]).) Then:
(a) [Regularity and gradient] $E$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$, of class $C^\infty$ on each of the open regions $\{|x|<a\}$, $\{|x|>a\}$; $\varphi\in C^1(\mathbb R^3)$, its displayed branch derivatives agree on $\{|x|=a\}$, and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]);
(b) [Classical equations] for every $x$ with $|x|\ne a$,
$$\operatorname{div}E(x)=\rho(x)/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E(x)=0$$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]);
(c) [Weak equations] the pair $(E,(\rho,0))$ satisfies the spatial distributional equations $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$: $E$ is $C^1$ on each side of the sphere $S_a=\{|x|=a\}$ with one-sided continuous traces that agree, $[E]=0$, so [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] gives
$$\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=\{\operatorname{curl}E\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[E]\,\delta_{S_a}=0,$$
with $\rho$ the displayed locally integrable density and no surface-charge term ([[def-em-weak-sources]], [[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]] for the sphere as a compact embedded smooth hypersurface); by the fixed-time reading of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] (e) these are the weak equations of the static model for this source, with zero singular part;
(d) [Energy] the field energy is finite and equals the assembly integral,
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\frac{3Q^2}{20\pi\varepsilon_0a},$$
computed with the polar formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]); the value agrees with the smooth-source identity of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] although the density here is only piecewise continuous;
